newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China enquires for March diesel but at low levels.
newsitem.headline: China enquires for March diesel but at low levels.

text.p: China buyers were starting to enquire for March-delivery diesel cargoes following the Lunar New Year holiday, but were indicating low bids as they were in no hurry to buy, industry sources said.
"There has been some enquiries but nothing has been done yet," a trader with an oil major said.
A Chinese trader said it was "a bit too early" to buy since many Chinese endusers were still away on holiday.
"They would not be in a rush to buy and would wait until prices fall to a level that they will be able to pay or when prices start to stabilise even more," he said.
Diesel stocks in China and Hong Kong were ample and endusers could easily have access to those barrels, he added.

A Chinese source said the country's diesel spot import purchases for March and subsequent months would be in the range of 400,000-500,000 tonnes a month, compared with more than 800,000 tonnes in November and December.
Traders said China was seeking to buy around $198-$200 per tonne, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to southern China.
Sellers were indicating around $204 a tonne, c-and-f.

They considered China's bids too low, especially since physical prices firmed slightly over the past week to $25.60 a barrel, free-on-board compared with $25.20 before the Lunar New Year. China bought some cargoes at around $200 per tonne, c-and-f before the holiday, which started on February 7, traders said.
At its peak late last year, diesel sales to China were around $263 a tonne, c-and-f, when fob Singapore prices reached a five-year high of $34.35 a barrel.
